verdict.rationale: Baseten documents its own first-party client libraries: the Performance Client in Python, JavaScript, and Rust for concurrent requests, and the Truss Python framework for packaging and deploying models. For general inference, though, the evidence shows Baseten relying on OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints called through third-party client SDKs rather than its own full SDK. Missing for 10: a documented general-purpose official SDK covering the platform API (deployments, training, usage), SDK reference docs and language coverage beyond the Performance Client's concurrent-request scope, and independent hands-on corroboration of SDK quality.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: The Performance Client sends concurrent requests from Python, JavaScript, or Rust.
Package your model's serving logic in Python, launch training jobs, and deploy to production—Truss handles containerization, dependency management, and GPU configuration.
They support the OpenAI Chat Completions API and the Anthropic Messages API in beta, so you can use familiar client SDKs.
